title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Knoxville, TN: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Knoxville and Oak Ridge nuclear, power plant, bridge and pipe inspectors: Part C choice, Part B travel and AWS eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Knoxville: Six Days for Oak Ridge Nuclear, TVA Power, Bridge and Pipe Welding Inspectors
html:
Knoxville workers can reach several major nuclear and power projects in the Tennessee Valley on a daily commute. At the Y-12 National Security Complex in Oak Ridge, the Uranium Processing Facility has entered its final construction phase. TVA received the first US construction permit for a BWRX-300 small modular reactor at its Clinch River site in September 2026, Kairos Power broke ground on its Hermes 2 reactor in April 2026, and Orano has signed an agreement with the building trades for a uranium enrichment plant in Oak Ridge. West of the city, TVA is building a gas plant to replace its Kingston coal units. All of it depends on welds, and every one of those welds has to be accepted by someone who can read the governing document and apply it.

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day preparation course for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination, written for East Tennessee welders, pipefitters, ironworkers, QC staff, NDT technicians and field engineers. The American Welding Society sets and administers the examination and issues the certification; you apply to AWS as an individual and must satisfy its education, experience and vision rules yourself. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has never seen AWS examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Knoxville. The six days can be followed online at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, delivered at an employer's site for a group, or booked one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. What each day covers is set out on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Five projects, five kinds of weld inspection work

The table summarizes what public reports said about each project at the time of writing and where a welding inspector usually fits. Schedules move and several depend on funding decisions, so read it as a map of the work rather than a hiring forecast.

ProjectLatest public reportWhere a welding inspector fits
Uranium Processing Facility, Y-12 National Security ComplexNNSA said in June 2025 that every UPF building was energized and the project had entered its last construction phase, with Bechtel delivering it and Consolidated Nuclear Security directing the work; four of seven subprojects were complete and about 2,500 people supported the project.Completion items, system testing and turnover, when weld records and inspection reports must be complete and traceable
Clinch River BWRX-300, TVAThe NRC issued the construction permit in September 2026 after a review of about 14 months; TVA had not announced a construction start and was still negotiating cost sharing with industry partners.Procurement and site preparation first, then a long build with both nuclear and conventional welding
Hermes and Hermes 2, Kairos Power, East Tennessee Technology ParkHermes construction began in 2024, and Hermes 2 broke ground on April 17, 2026, with operation expected by 2030.Receiving and site assembly of reactor modules built at the company's Albuquerque campus, plus plant steel and piping
Project IKE, Orano, Oak RidgeOrano signed a memorandum of understanding with North America's Building Trades Unions in April 2026; construction is expected to employ more than 1,000 workers, with enrichment starting in the early 2030s.Building steel, process and utility piping, and supplier surveillance once construction begins
Kingston gas plant, TVAA 1,500-megawatt plant under construction to replace the Kingston coal plant in 2027, with about 1,200 construction workers, according to a May 2025 report.Fuel and auxiliary piping, structural steel and equipment supports during erection and commissioning

Nuclear sites: where the CWI helps and where project rules take over

Safety-related welding at a nuclear facility is controlled by the project's quality assurance program and the code that program commits to, most often the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code for pressure-retaining items. Those documents decide who may perform, record and accept weld examinations, and the qualification they ask for is normally issued under the employer's own written practice rather than by AWS. A CWI does not replace it. What the CWI gives a Knoxville inspector is a recognized, portable grounding in welding processes, symbols, procedure and qualification records, metallurgy and discontinuities, which is the knowledge a nuclear QC program builds on.

Plenty of the welding on these jobs is conventional anyway: building steel, pipe racks, supports, tanks and utility systems outside the safety-related scope. There the structural and piping codes apply in the familiar way, and contractors often make a CWI responsible for welding quality. Kairos Power adds a twist worth noting. The American Nuclear Society reported that its reactor equipment modules are fabricated in Albuquerque, New Mexico, then shipped to Oak Ridge for assembly, so some inspection happens in a distant shop and some during site fit-up. Source inspection and receiving inspection of fabricated modules reward symbol reading, dimensional checks and record review as much as watching an arc. For the NDT side of nuclear work, see nuclear NDT training for Oak Ridge.

Kingston and the power side of the valley

Gas plant construction is pipe-heavy work. Fuel gas, lubricating oil and auxiliary systems in a gas-fired station are commonly built to ASME B31.1, Power Piping, with procedures and welders qualified to ASME Section IX, while the steel around the units and inside the buildings follows AWS D1.1 or the owner's structural specification. The May 2025 report described the Kingston units as aeroderivative turbines able to start in about four minutes and said roughly 35 people would run the finished plant. For a pipe welder working toward inspection, a project like this is a good place to build documented welding-related experience, and the ASME option for Part C, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, matches the paperwork on the job.

Bridges and the West Knoxville corridor

Interstate work west of the city is moving from study toward projects. In November 2026 TDOT released the recommended alternatives from its Planning and Environment Linkages study of about 17 miles of I-40 and I-75, between the I-40/I-75 interchange in Loudon County and I-640, and asked for public comment. TDOT stated plainly that the recommendations are not yet funded commitments. When interstate jobs of that size are built, steel girders, bearings and attachments for new bridges are generally fabricated to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, whose Clause 12 deals with fracture-critical members, with the owner's specifications layered on top.

A candidate who expects to work for a bridge fabricator, or for the inspection consultants a state DOT hires to watch fabrication and erection, should look hard at D1.5 for Part C. Background reading: AWS D1.5.

Picking a Part C code book in East Tennessee

AWS lets each candidate choose the book for Part C, an open-book test of 50 to 65 questions. The editions below are the ones the AWS CWI page listed in November 2026, matched to common Knoxville-area jobs:

  • ASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3 (2023, 2024 and 2024 editions): gas plant piping at Kingston, process piping at Y-12 and Project IKE, and pipe crews moving between power and process work.
  • AWS D1.1, 2020 edition: building steel, pipe racks, platforms and equipment supports on every project in the table above.
  • AWS D1.5, 2020 edition including Clause 12: bridge fabrication and repair for TDOT and local agencies.
  • API 1104, 22nd edition: gas transmission and distribution pipeline contractors.
  • AWS D1.2, 2014 edition: aluminum structures and fabrication.

The exam editions can trail the copies on your desk at work, and tables and clause numbers shift between editions, so study the one AWS names. If your work spans structural steel and pipe, pick the book you expect to use most over the next several years rather than the one that looks easiest. More reading: ASME Section IX, ASME B31.1 and AWS D1.1.

Turning East Tennessee experience into an AWS application

Under its QC1 specification AWS trades formal education against documented welding-related experience. A high school diploma calls for five years, completed trade or vocational courses for four, and an associate degree or higher in engineering technology, engineering or physical science for two. AWS decides what counts, so describe duties, not job titles. Four hypothetical Knoxville candidates show how the rules play out:

  • A TCAT Knoxville combination welding graduate with three years on structural and pipe crews. The vocational line asks for four years, so this candidate is a year short and could keep building experience or look at the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) first.
  • A pipefitter with a high school diploma and six years on power and process piping projects. That clears the five-year line, provided every contractor can confirm the dates and the welding-related duties.
  • A UT technician certified by an employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, with four years examining welds on fabricated modules after a completed technical program. Whether NDT years count as welding-related is AWS's call, and a clear description of the weld-related duties helps.
  • A mechanical engineer with a bachelor's degree working as a field engineer on a nuclear construction job. The engineering-degree line asks for two years, documented through the procedures, inspection plans and weld records the engineer handled.

Write the record the way an assessor reads it: employer, dates, processes and materials, the codes or specifications followed, and any inspection, documentation or qualification-test duties, each with a person who can confirm them. You also need to pass the AWS vision test, recorded on the AWS visual acuity form, timed so the result is current when you sit the exam. For more on how AWS reads an application, see the CWI requirements guide.

TCAT Knoxville and the AWS sections in reach

Tennessee College of Applied Technology Knoxville runs a full-time welding technology program of 1,296 clock hours, normally about 12 months across three trimesters, with day and night classes at its Liberty Street campus. It teaches flame cutting, shielded metal arc, gas tungsten arc, gas metal arc and flux cored arc welding along with pipe welding, and lists AWS plate and pipe welder certifications up to 6G pipe. Graduates of a diploma program like this one usually apply under the trade or vocational experience line, though AWS makes that call.

For section activity, the AWS Holston Valley Section met in Kingsport in January 2026 and held a March meeting with a presentation on laser scanning of weld joints and finished profiles, and the AWS Chattanooga Section belongs to District 8. Neither section's site says which counties it serves, so use the section finder on aws.org to locate the one meeting closest to you.

Getting to Part B from Knoxville

Parts A and C are computer-based tests taken at Prometric centers once AWS accepts your application. Part B, the practical, is run by AWS at its seminar locations. The AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 named no Tennessee city; the listed sites nearest East Tennessee included Kennesaw, Georgia, and Birmingham, Alabama, with Indianapolis and Cleveland also on the list. Check the AWS seminar and exam schedule for the Part B dates tied to each site. US applications are due six weeks before the Part B date, and each part needs a score of at least 72 percent, so build in travel, a night away and room for a possible retake. The CWI exam cost calculator helps with the budget.

In Part B you handle tools, specimens and documents supplied by AWS and answer 46 questions about them. Put practice time into measuring fillet size, convexity, undercut and misalignment until the gauge readings are automatic, and into reading a procedure to decide whether the conditions you are shown fall inside it.

Fitting six days around shifts and outages

Many Knoxville candidates work rotating construction shifts or long outage stretches. The online format spreads the six days of material across evenings and days off, with the instructor answering questions in writing as you go. One workable rhythm is to finish the fundamentals block before the application goes in, work through the code book while AWS reviews it, and save the timed practice papers for the final fortnight before Part A. One-to-one sessions suit a candidate who needs focused help on one part, or who wants the six days fitted into a break between projects.

When a contractor brings the six days to its site

A mechanical contractor, fabricator or construction manager with several candidates can host the course at its yard or project office. The group then practises on its own weld samples with its own gauges, and the Part C work can follow the code most of the group will choose. Employers often time it ahead of a new scope so that fresh inspectors hold the credential before they are needed. Every candidate still applies to AWS personally, with their own vision record and experience evidence.

After the CWI

AWS keeps a CWI valid for nine years, with renewal applications due at years three and six. At the nine-year point AWS offers recertification through 80 professional development hours, a fresh pass of Part B, or its Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential. Many Knoxville CWIs also add NDT methods, which the employer certifies under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including VT Level 2, UT Level 2, MT Level 2 and PT Level 2, and the employer certifies afterward. Inspectors who move toward operating plants sometimes add an API individual certification such as API 510 or API 570; Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation, and API administers those examinations and certifies inspectors.

Local pages: NDT training in Knoxville, ultrasonic testing in Knoxville, Practical NDT simulator access from Knoxville, and CWI exam prep in Nashville, Atlanta and Birmingham.

Sending a Knoxville enquiry

Tell us the format you want, how many people need preparation, the Part C code each one plans to use and roughly when they intend to sit the exam. For a group, include the site and the weeks that avoid outages, mobilizations or system turnover. If an experience record looks borderline, describe it and we will point out what to confirm with AWS. Each format is quoted on request, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Knoxville?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Knoxville. You study online at your own pace, at your employer's site as part of a group, or one-to-one online or in person at a location agreed when you book. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: Does a CWI let me inspect safety-related welds at Y-12 or on a reactor project?
faq.a: Not by itself. Safety-related work is governed by the project's quality assurance program and the code it follows, and those set the qualification for examination personnel. The CWI is a strong foundation, but the project decides who may perform and sign weld examinations.

faq.q: Which Part C code book fits work at the Kingston gas plant?
faq.a: Usually the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because power plant piping and welder qualification are written around those documents. Pick AWS D1.1 instead if most of your work is structural steel.

faq.q: Can I take Part B in Tennessee?
faq.a: The AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 named no Tennessee city. Sites nearer East Tennessee included Kennesaw, Georgia, and Birmingham, Alabama. Check the AWS seminar and exam schedule for Part B dates at each site.

faq.q: I finished the TCAT Knoxville welding diploma. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational courses put you on the four-year line in the AWS table, as long as AWS accepts the program and the work as welding-related. Keep employer contacts who can confirm your dates and duties.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Knoxville?
faq.a: We could not confirm a section that meets in Knoxville itself. The Holston Valley Section met in Kingsport in 2026, and the Chattanooga Section is part of District 8. The section finder on aws.org shows the nearest one.

faq.q: Can a contractor working in Oak Ridge host the six days for its QC staff?
faq.a: Yes. Under the corporate format the six days are delivered at the contractor's yard or project office, using its own samples and gauges. Each person still applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Has AWS approved or endorsed this course?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has no access to AWS examination content or results. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I ask for a quote from Knoxville?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page and give the format, the number of candidates and the Part C code. We send a quote on request for the format you pick and reply within one business day.
